summary: Oversized leaf: the spec bundles three independently testable, independently shippable behaviors - (1) per-band depth-based mixing in AudioSystem (high-frequency roll-off, low-frequency pressure rumble, altered reverb, parameters expressed as content data), (2) creature sound profiles from the section 58 vocabulary for every ST-03 major creature with per-band pre-visibility cue lead times tuned against final band visibility, and (3) sparse music tied to existing trigger flags with no 90-second loop. The behavior field is a four-item run-on, AC-art-sound merges all three, and the verification lists three separate browser scenarios (depth ladder, creature encounter lead time, music placement) plus two Node assertion groups; each deliverable ships and proves without the others - the same shape the WI-06d split applied. The two named changed responsibilities are within the three limit, so the failure is the behavior count. What is sound and must be preserved on the children: depends_on [WI-06a, WI-06b, WI-06c] (lead times measured against settled band visibility), AC-art-sound carried verbatim with per-part proof and one named final proof owner, the save.settings.masterVolume seam kept working, the no-new-gameplay-rules boundary (cues read the existing trigger seam - TriggerState.audioCues/playAudio already exist in src/world/triggers.ts), extend-not-rebuild on AudioSystem (AudioSnapshot already exposes depth, masterVolume, highCutoff, lowRumble, reverb), procedural WebAudio with no large sampled assets, and the section 70 spoiler rule. Useful split boundary (promote to a story keeping id WI-06e, leaves WI-06e-a/b/c, all inheriting depends_on [WI-06a, WI-06b, WI-06c] and carrying AC-art-sound verbatim): WI-06e-a depth-based mixing (depth-ladder browser inspection + monotonic-curve Node test); WI-06e-b creature profiles and pre-visibility cues (encounter lead-time check against final visibility + profile Node test); WI-06e-c sparse music (placement pass, no loop), named final proof owner of the full AC-art-sound. Revision gap to close before the split can be filed: as inventoried every leaf would change both named subsystems, so the revision must re-attribute the per-leaf data-seam ownership (band mixing parameters, creature profile data, music placement data) so each leaf carries a strict subset of the parent's changed subsystems, then split. Handoff, non-goals and per-behavior evidence are otherwise fresh-session ready.
